blocks.h2: What to Do When a Pipe Bursts
blocks.intro: Do these three things first. They limit the damage while we're on the way.

steps.body: Your main shutoff valve is usually near the water meter in the basement or a utility room. Turn it clockwise to stop water to the whole house.
If water is near outlets, appliances or your electrical panel, stay out of the water and turn off power to that area only if you can do it safely.
Our phone line is open nights, weekends and holidays. Tell us where the water is coming from and we'll take it from there.

blocks.intro: A burst pipe isn't always water spraying across the basement. When a pipe splits inside a wall, a ceiling or under a floor, the signs are quieter: stains, bubbling paint, warped floors and a water bill that suddenly jumps. Here's where to look:

bullets: Yellow, brown or dark water stains on plaster, drywall or ceiling panels.
Paint that bubbles, cracks or flakes, or wallpaper that starts to peel.
Drywall or plaster that sags, bows or feels soft to the touch.
Mold or mildew along baseboards and in wall corners.
Hardwood that cups or buckles, or laminate and vinyl that lifts.
Wood baseboards that swell, crack or lose their paint.
Puddles on the floor, drips from the ceiling or water coming out from under cabinets and vanities.
Water spraying, dripping or gushing from a crack, joint or pinhole.
A hissing sound near a pipe.
Wet spots or puddles under pipes in the basement or crawl space.
A water bill that jumps with no change in how you use water.
The sound of running water when every fixture is off.
A water meter that keeps moving when nothing is running.

blocks.note: Seeing water come from a wall or ceiling? Shut off the main and call us 24/7, even if you're not sure it's a burst pipe.

blocks.intro: A frozen pipe almost always gives you a warning before it bursts. As the water inside freezes, pressure builds until the pipe splits, and the leak usually shows up once it thaws. Watch for these signs during a cold snap:

tiles.h3: No Water or Just a Trickle
tiles.body: A faucet that gives you nothing, or a thin trickle, on a very cold day usually means the pipe feeding it has frozen somewhere along the way.

tiles.h3: Frost or Ice on the Pipe
tiles.body: Frost, ice or heavy condensation on pipes in a basement, crawl space or garage is a pipe on the edge of freezing solid.
A visible bulge or hairline split in an exposed pipe means the ice has already stretched it. It may hold until it thaws, then leak.

blocks.note: Think a pipe is frozen? Keep the faucet open, never thaw it with an open flame, and call us before it thaws and splits.

blocks.h2: Why Pipes Freeze in Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: Lake County winters bring long stretches below freezing, and about 1 in 4 Highland Park homes was built before 1940. That combination is hard on pipes.

items.h3: Pipes in Exterior Walls and Crawl Spaces
items.body: Pipes in exterior walls, crawl spaces, garages and outdoor spigot lines freeze first. Older homes often have plumbing in spots that weren't insulated the way they would be today.
A hose left connected in winter traps water in the spigot line, and that water freezes and splits the pipe inside the wall. It often isn't found until the spring thaw.

Galvanized steel and older copper lines are already thinner or corroded after decades of use, so a freeze is more likely to split them. If breaks keep happening, it may be time to talk about the pipes themselves.

blocks.h2: Burst Pipe Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: How do I keep my pipes from freezing in winter?
items.preview: Disconnect hoses, keep the heat on, open sink cabinets on exterior walls and let a faucet drip.
items.answer: Disconnect garden hoses and shut off and drain outdoor spigots in the fall. Keep the heat on, even when you're away. On the coldest nights, open cabinet doors under sinks on exterior walls and let a faucet drip. Insulating pipes in crawl spaces and garages helps too.

items.q: What should I do if I think a pipe is frozen?
items.preview: Keep the faucet open, never use an open flame, and call before it splits.
items.answer: Keep the faucet open so water can flow once it thaws. Never use an open flame to thaw a pipe. If you can't find the frozen section, or it's inside a wall, call us before it splits.

items.q: Does homeowners insurance cover a burst pipe?
items.preview: Sudden bursts are often covered. Check your policy. We can document the cause.
items.answer: A sudden, accidental pipe burst is often covered by a standard policy, while damage from a slow leak or lack of maintenance may not be. Check your policy or ask your insurer. We can document the cause of the break, which may support your claim.

items.q: How much does burst pipe repair cost?
items.preview: It depends on the location and pipe. You get a flat-rate price before any work begins.
items.answer: It depends on where the break is, how easy it is to reach, the pipe material and how much of the pipe needs replacing. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins. Financing is available.
